import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Drop rows where 'embark_town' is missing to ensure clean facets
df.dropna(subset=['embark_town'], inplace=True)

# Map pclass to more descriptive labels for the plot
df['pclass_str'] = df['pclass'].map({1: 'First Class', 2: 'Second Class', 3: 'Third Class'})

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)

# Create a FacetGrid to show survival rate across multiple categories
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='pclass_str',
    y='survived',
    hue='sex',
    col='embark_town',
    kind='bar',
    palette='viridis',
    height=5,
    aspect=1.2,
    order=['First Class', 'Second Class', 'Third Class'],
    legend=False  # We will add a custom legend
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set overall title and adjust its position
g.fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Rate by Class, Sex, and Port of Embarkation', fontsize=20, y=1.03)

# Set axis labels for clarity
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Rate")

# Format the y-axis to show percentages
for ax in g.axes.flat:
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=1.0))
    ax.margins(y=0.1) # Add a little space at the top of the bars

# Set titles for each subplot (facet)
g.set_titles("Embarked: {col_name}", size=14)

# Add a clear, well-placed legend
g.add_legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right', bbox_to_anchor=(0.95, 0.95))

# Add annotations to the bars to show the exact survival rate
for ax in g.axes.flat:
    for p in ax.patches:
        ax.annotate(f"{p.get_height():.0%}",
                    (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
                    ha='center', va='center',
                    xytext=(0, 9),
                    textcoords='offset points',
                    fontsize=10,
                    color='black')

# Adjust layout to prevent title overlap
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
